rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with the provided 3BB grade, but it overstates image-confirmable detail such as a clearly enlarged blastocoel occupying most of the embryo and a distinctly identifiable ICM in the upper-left; the image is somewhat indistinct and supports only a moderate-quality blastocyst with loose ICM/TE rather than such precise localization.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrium, cycle history, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with the prognosis broadly matching the case; however, some quantitative claims and adjustments are somewhat speculative and more confident than the evidence supports.

Mostly aligned on SET and general prognosis, but there are notable deviations: calling grade 3 an 'expanded blastocyst' is inconsistent with standard Gardner terminology, recommending routine estradiol addition is not standard, and suggesting PGT-A on cryopreserved embryos via warming-biopsy-refreeze is not routine first-line guidance for a 31-year-old first cycle.

Provides clear practical recommendations for SET, luteal support, OHSS monitoring, follow-up testing, and future planning, though some suggestions are broader than necessary and a few are not tightly case-specific.
